Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant® American Express® Card and Bevy Card: Bonus Points Plus Statement Credits, Limited Time

by Chris Carley
August 10, 2026
in Credit Cards, Hotels
0

Two Marriott Bonvoy cards are running elevated limited-time welcome offers through September 30, 2026, and both do something the usual Marriott promotions don’t: they pair bonus points with a statement credit. The Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant® American Express® Card carries the bigger offer and the bigger annual fee. The Marriott Bonvoy Bevy® American Express® Card asks less on both counts. Which one fits comes down to whether you’ll actually use a Free Night Award every year — and, just as important, whether you’re even eligible.

(Terms apply to American Express benefits and offers. Enrollment may be required for select American Express benefits and offers. Visit americanexpress.com to learn more.)

Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant® American Express® Card

Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant® American Express® Card

  • Earn 150,000 bonus Marriott Bonvoy® points plus a $250 statement credit after you spend $6,000 in eligible purchases within the first six (6) months of being approved for card membership. Offer expires September 30, 2026. (Terms apply.)
  • Annual fee: $650 (Rates & Fees)
  • Read more and learn how to apply →

The Brilliant is the top of the Marriott lineup, and the offer reflects it. The spending requirement works out to $1,000 a month for six months — steady but not trivial.

What you’re buying beyond the bonus: complimentary Marriott Bonvoy Platinum Elite status, an annual Free Night Award starting in year two good at properties up to 85,000 points, up to $300 a year in dining credits, and Priority Pass™™ Select membership. The $650 annual fee (Rates & Fees) is real money, and whether the card survives year two depends almost entirely on whether that Free Night Award gets used.

Marriott Bonvoy Bevy® American Express® Card

Marriott Bonvoy Bevy® American Express® Card

  • Earn 125,000 bonus Marriott Bonvoy® points plus a $150 statement credit after you spend $5,000 in eligible purchases within the first six (6) months of being approved for card membership. Offer expires September 30, 2026. (Terms apply.)
  • Annual fee: $250 (Rates & Fees)
  • Read more and learn how to apply →

The Bevy is the middle child: Gold Elite status instead of Platinum, no automatic annual Free Night Award, and a lower bar to clear on the welcome offer.

Its best everyday feature is the earning structure — 4X Marriott Bonvoy® points at restaurants worldwide and U.S. supermarkets, on up to $15,000 in combined purchases per calendar year, then 2X Marriott Bonvoy® points. That’s genuinely useful spend, which is more than most hotel cards manage. The catch is year two: at a $250 annual fee (Rates & Fees) with no automatic Free Night Award, you have to spend $15,000 in a calendar year to earn one. That’s a lot of asking.

Check Your Eligibility Before You Apply

This is the part that trips people up, and it’s stricter than most readers expect. Beyond the usual “you can’t have had this card before” language, the welcome offers on both cards are unavailable to anyone who:

  • Has held certain Ritz-Carlton or legacy Starwood cards in the last 30 days
  • Has acquired a Marriott Bonvoy Bountiful, Boundless, or Bold card from Chase in the last 90 days
  • Has received a new cardmember bonus on a Marriott Bonvoy Bountiful, Boundless, or Bold card from Chase in the last 24 months

That last one catches a lot of people. A Chase Marriott bonus two years ago can still block you today, and it applies across issuers — Amex and Chase coordinate on this. The Bevy adds a longer list of disqualifying Chase products than the Brilliant does, so being eligible for one doesn’t guarantee eligibility for the other.

The good news: American Express tells you before it processes your application, so you get the chance to withdraw rather than eat a hard pull for nothing. Still worth reading the offer terms first.

Which One Makes Sense

The Brilliant if Marriott is genuinely your hotel program. Platinum status changes how your stays feel — suite upgrades when available, lounge access, late checkout — and the annual Free Night Award at up to 85,000 points can be worth several hundred dollars on its own if you book it somewhere expensive. This is a card that rewards people who already stay at Marriott properties and would be there anyway.

The Bevy if you want a large pile of Marriott Bonvoy® points without committing $650 a year to find out whether you’ll use the perks. Lower spending requirement, lower annual fee, and the restaurant and supermarket earning does work between hotel stays.

Neither if Marriott isn’t where you stay. A six-figure Bonvoy balance in a program you don’t use is a number, not a vacation — and Marriott’s award pricing is dynamic, so those points buy less than they used to. And don’t create spending you wouldn’t otherwise have to hit a threshold. A bonus you financed at 20-plus percent interest isn’t a bonus.

There’s also a third Marriott card worth knowing about — the business version, with a lower annual fee and an offer that isn’t going anywhere at the end of September. We break down all three cards in depth — earning rates, benefits, and the fine print on every credit — in our complete Marriott Bonvoy card guide.

Learn here how to apply for the Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant™ American Express® Card

Learn here how to apply for the Marriott Bonvoy Bevy American Express Card

Final Approach

Bonvoy points aren’t what they were. I’m not going to pretend otherwise, and anyone who tells you a Marriott point is worth what it was in 2019 is selling something. But the fifth-night-free benefit on award stays quietly stretches a big balance further than the raw number suggests, and a statement credit on top of the points is a genuinely better structure than the usual points-only promotion.

I’ve hit my card limit with the issuer and can’t get the Brilliant. I’ve tried. It’s still the one I’d pick.

Both offers run through September 30, 2026 — which sounds like plenty of time right up until it isn’t.

More current offers live on our best welcome offers page, and you can compare these against other hotel cards on our hotel credit card recommendations page.
